Subject: Post-call recap: Novamed dedicated capacity — prioritized pain points & SLA trade-offs

Alex — thanks again for the time today. Below is a short recap of what we heard, our suggested next steps, and a rough trade-off matrix for the SLA/ isolation options we discussed. Attaching the one-pager and a draft mutual action plan for your procurement team.

Summary of customer goals / pain points (from today's call):
- Latency sensitivity: sub-150ms tail for inference on clinical triage model (95th percentile) during business hours.
- Strong data isolation requirements (PHI, HITRUST-aligned controls) — preference for isolated dedicated pools or VPC-private deployment.
- Predictable cost: need monthly committed capacity to show predictable unit economics to finance.
- Scalability: expect baseline 10 rps (requests/sec) with spikes to 60 rps during batch ingest windows; peaks can be up to 120 rps for short bursts.
- Rollout constraints: phased canary (10% -> 50% -> 100%), automated fallback to smaller model if latency or capacity breached.

Technical constraints and assumptions we captured:
- Model: quantized LLM (7B family) with ~2k token average inference; KV cache possible for common prefixes.
- Target throughput: sustained 10 rps equivalent / need capacity to burst to 120 rps for ~5-10 minute windows.
- Isolation: single-tenant reserved GPU pool preferred; optional VPC private control plane for on-preming compliance.

SLA / trade-offs (high level):
- Option A (Standard reserved pool + tenant isolation): 99.9% uptime SLA; typical 95th latency ~120–160ms; lower cost per token vs fully private.
- Option B (Dedicated single-tenant + VPC): 99.95% uptime SLA; stronger network isolation & audit hooks; ~10–15% premium on monthly commit.
- Option C (On-prem/private appliance): 99.95% SLA (customer infra dependent); highest control, highest TCO and procurement lead time.

Immediate next steps (proposed):
1) Redwood to share: one-pager (attached) + MAP spreadsheet with proposed phasing and milestone owners (attached).
2) Novamed to confirm: preferred isolation tier (A|B|C) and a target monthly commit range (GPU-hours or seats).
3) Tech sync: schedule a 60-minute ops deep-dive with Ben (infrastructure) and Marissa (SRE/Onboard) to validate throughput and fallback behaviors.
4) Procurement: if moving forward, provide primary procurement contact and any MSA constraints (data residency, SOC2 evidence, KMS requirements).

Trade-off note: If Novamed prioritizes sub-150ms p95 during business hours and strict PHI isolation, Option B is the balanced path — slightly higher cost but reduces risk and shortens time-to-onboard compared to full on-prem.

Alex — answers inline below. Looping Ben and Marissa to set the ops sync.

1) Burst handling: our reserved pools support burst capacity via two mechanisms: a) pre-warmed standby instances in the pool that are routed for short bursts (seconds to a few minutes) and b) autoscaling with a fast-path for short-lived scheduling that brings additional instances online within ~45–90s depending on the model size. For noisy bursts that exceed reserved standby, our fallback policy can route to a quantized smaller model to preserve latency SLOs. We'll capture exact warm-up behavior in the ops deep-dive and include benchmark runs.

2) Pricing premium (ballpark): Option B (VPC + dedicated single-tenant) typically runs ~8–14% higher than Option A for the same committed GPU-hours, depending on network isolation and audit log retention cadence. Option C (on-prem) is very variable — expect +25–60% TCO difference when you factor infra + O&M. We'll include formal ranges in the commercial sheet.

3) KMS: yes — we support customer-managed keys (AWS KMS / GCP KMS) within the VPC offering. Lead time is usually 2–3 weeks to wire key access and run an initial key rotation test; we can accelerate with your security team.

Ops sync proposal: Ben and Marissa are available next week. Suggested slots: Tue 15 Jun 10:30–11:30 PT or Wed 16 Jun 09:00–10:00 PT. Agenda: benchmark targets, warm-up behavior, canary plan and rollback triggers, KMS integration steps.
